TITLE: Controlled Evaluation of Semi-structured Representations for Table QA
PROPOSAL: Develop a joint benchmark suite, Structured-Semi, consisting of 5 datasets with the same information represented in both structured and semi-structured formats. Utilize the WikiSQL, Spider (for text-to-SQL DB querying), and WebQuestions (for web table QA) datasets, modifying them to preserve column semantics but alter table structures. Create a balanced set of queries, including lookups, aggregations, and multi-step reasoning, to test model adaptability across representations.
CONTROLS: Baseline implementation of NL2SQL, LLM-based, and hybrid methods on the original datasets, as well as a null model that always predicts the most frequent query answer from the training data.

PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial evaluation framework, AdVersa, to systematically probe the robustness of Table QA models against noise and incompleteness in semi-structured tables. Construct a new set of synthetic datasets with manually introduced biases, missing headers, misplaced values, and mixed metadata types, carefully simulating real-world challenges like inconsistent formatting.
